newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks rise for third consecutive day.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks rise for third consecutive day.

text.p: Caracas stocks rose in light trade for the third straight session, carried forward on the momentum of the bolsa's gains last week plus the prospect of strong economic growth in 1997, traders said.
Last week government ministers said the economy would grow by four percent in 1997 and by more than six percent from 1998 forward.

The market's leading index edged ahead 0.65 percent to close at 6,250.01. Twenty shares rose, 13 fell and six closed flat. A total of 32.4 million shares traded, worth 2.4 billion bolivars ($5 million).
"Trade was very light and I don't see a trend for the coming week. There'll be rises some days and falls others but no important movements," said Financorp broker Hector Perez.
The single most important event in the calender before Christmas is the auction of state-owned banks Banco de Venezuela and Banco Consolidado on Thursday, traders added.

Among widely-held stocks, Electricidad de Caracas gained 9.00 bolivars to close at 534.00, telephone company Cantv gained 30 bolivars to end at 1775.00, while Mavesa rose 3.95 bolivars to end at 144.95.
